subject: Request: hosted API baseline + burst tier structure for Q3 pilot
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena.park@nimbusretail.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot pricing request — baseline + burst tiers

Hi Priya,

Following up from our call last week — Nimbus Retail is planning a Q3 pilot for product search and personalization that will hit roughly 1.2B tokens/month baseline with expected spikes up to 3–4B tokens in promotional windows. Procurement asked me to get a clear hosted API baseline and the burst tiering options so we can model cost for the pilot.

Could you share: 1) standard hosted API baseline unit price for text-gen tokens (per-token or per-1k) and typical tier breakpoints, 2) a burst pricing model (how burst capacity is priced and any hourly/crediting mechanics), 3) pilot discounts or short-term credits for a 3-month proof-of-value, and 4) any SLA/crediting language that applies to high-throughput usage.

I've attached a short spreadsheet with our expected usage profile and ideal start window (Nimbus_MA_Pricing_Request.xlsx). We need this back by end of week to feed our internal budget.

Thanks — happy to hop on 30 min call if helpful.

Best,
Lena
Lena Park
Head of Data Science, Nimbus Retail

Attachment: Nimbus_MA_Pricing_Request.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 11:03:22 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing request — baseline + burst tiers

Hi Lena — thanks for the note and the spreadsheet. Looping in Ben (pricing lead) and Priyom (solutions) so we can align on a proposal.

Quick summary we can send today:
- Baseline hosted API: $0.0009 per token (billed per 1k tokens = $0.90/1k) for month-to-month usage.
- Volume tiers (hosted) with step discounts applied to incremental consumption:
  * 0–250M tokens: $0.00090/token
  * 250M–1B: $0.00078/token
  * 1B–3B: $0.00060/token
  * >3B: custom pricing / quoted (typically 15–30% below 1B–3B band depending on commit)
- Burst capacity: we offer burst credits purchased as hourly throughput credits (e.g., 1 GPU-hour equivalent = X tokens) or as a prepaid burst bucket. For short spikes we recommend the prepaid burst bucket for predictable unit economics. Hourly burst pricing is ~1.5x the baseline per-token cost for on-demand.
- Pilot discount: we can offer a limited 20% pilot credit on baseline unit price for the first 3 months if Nimbus commits to a minimum 3-month trial and shares latency/traffic profiles. Pilot credits apply only to hosted API token charges, not to add-ons (observability retention, private deployment setup).
- SLA/credits: standard hosted SLA applies; we provide service credits for availability <99.9% per month pro-rated. For sustained high-throughput we can propose elevated SLOs for Dedicated or Reserved plans.

I'm attaching our public rate card PDF and I'll follow up with a short internal note suggesting an adjusted committed rate if you can commit to a 6–12 month volume band.

Next steps: if this looks close, I can send a one-page proposal and a DocuSign for a pilot addendum.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
priay.natarajan@redwood.com

Attachment: Redwood_Hosted_RateCard_Q1-2027.pdf (pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 15:28:10 -0800
Subject: Internal: Nimbus pricing — margin check and suggested committed option

Priya / Priyom — saw your draft numbers. A couple of notes:
1) If they truly do 1.2B baseline with 3–4B spikes, we should push for a committed baseline at $0.00075/token for a 6-month commit. That keeps gross margin acceptable while giving them meaningful savings vs month-to-month.
2) For burst economics, offer the prepaid burst bucket with a 25% discount vs on-demand hourly pricing if they prepay a 1-month burst budget. That reduces surprise costs and keeps throughput predictable.
3) Pilot credit: 20% is fine, but make it a dollar-denominated credit (e.g., $150k in consumption credit) for the 3-month pilot to simplify procurement/legal.

Can we get an updated proposal with the committed 6-month band and the dollar credit? If legal needs to keep an escape, add a 30-day termination for convenience during pilot.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts

(Internal only comment included: need margin sign-off from finance before shipping committed 6-month pricing.)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 10:09:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing request — baseline + burst tiers

Hi Lena — thanks, and appreciate the fast turnaround. Based on internal alignment we've drafted a short proposal and attached the one-page PDF (redwood_proposal_D-2027-0482.pdf). Summary of the updated proposal: 

- Committed baseline pilot: $0.00075/token for a 6-month committed baseline set at 1.2B tokens/month.
- Pilot credit: $150,000 in consumption credit applied across the first 3 months to offset spikes; credits apply to hosted API token charges.
- Burst bucket: prepaid monthly burst bucket priced at $0.00095/token (25% off on-demand hourly rate), recommended purchase = 450M tokens/month to cover anticipated spikes. Unused prepaid burst credits roll forward for 30 days.
- SLA: standard hosted SLA included; for anything higher we can scope Dedicated as a follow-on.

If that aligns, we'll send a DocuSign for the pilot addendum (no long-term lock beyond the 6-month commit) and provide a short implementation checklist (API keys, rate-limit adjustments, telemetry hooks). Please confirm by Fri 19 Feb so we can schedule provisioning.

Best,
Priya

Attachment: redwood_proposal_D-2027-0482.pdf

On Mon, Feb 15, 2027 at 09:12 AM Lena Park <lena.park@nimbusretail.com> wrote:
> Following up from our call last week — Nimbus Retail is planning a Q3 pilot...
> (original message quoted)

From: Lena Park <lena.park@nimbusretail.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbusretail.com
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 17:42:07 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing request — baseline + burst tiers

Priya / Ben — thanks, this is much closer to what procurement needs. A few clarifying questions before we sign: 

1) For the prepaid burst bucket, what happens if we exceed the purchased monthly burst tokens? Is additional consumption billed at the on-demand hourly rate (confirm price), or do you throttle?
2) Can we convert the $150k pilot credit into monthly consumption credits applied in order (month 1 then month 2, etc.) rather than a lump sum? Procurement prefers monthly application to match invoicing.
3) Any SLA credit thresholds tied to high-throughput incidents (e.g., if a spike causes errors and impacts business, what's the remediation/crediting cadence)?

We also attached a redline (attached) to the one-pager with a few legal asks around liability and data retention. If you prefer, we can take a short 30 min call tomorrow to go through.

Lena
Head of Data Science, Nimbus Retail

Attachment: Nimbus_redline_proposal_v1.docx (docx)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 18:05:30 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing request — baseline + burst tiers

Thanks Lena — quick answers: 
- Excess burst: billed at on-demand hourly rate ($0.00127/token equivalent) above the prepaid bucket; we do not throttle automatically but will send alerts and can enable soft limits on provisioning.
- Credit application: we can apply the $150k as monthly consumption credits (split across first 3 months) — we will reflect that in DocuSign.
- SLA for spikes: standard hosted SLA applies; for operational incidents caused by burst overload we offer accelerated incident response and pro-rated service credits; we'll surface the exact credit calculation in the addendum.

I'll have legal and billing include the redline responses and circulate a DocuSign today. Thanks for the redlines — we'll review and call if needed.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
priay.natarajan@redwood.com

(Internal note: loop Neha for billing setup and Priyom for provisioning playbook.)
